changed.what: Step 3 stated the E7-K1/E7-K2 scan entries with conditions the N38b-50 engine cannot express ('unless labelled uncentred', 'without the exact 0.55 m beside it'), so the legitimate rows of the GB-04 and GB-05 card files (walk set registries/) would fire from M0. Now engine-form entries (with a leading \b), the stale-as-control markers on the card rows and test lines, and an acceptance item plus a unit test (e7k_stale_entries_marked) that a planted unmarked line fires and the cards do not.

Script step 4 ran `cargo test -p frob-scene purity`; no test name contains 'purity', so it ran nothing and exited 0. Now it names the tests, `-- pack_is_pure_procedural starter_pack_regenerates_bit_identical`, and asserts that four ran. Added the missing pack_is_pure_procedural_starter_pack test that acceptance item 3 needs.

The refusals are now named from N19-REF: al-infi-1 gives asset-source-not-default-pipeline (ASSET_SOURCE_NOT_DEFAULT, interim 802, exit 3, nothing written); an output set without its record (al-infi-3) gives FROB-REF-303. Acceptance updated to match.

With the notice removed the entry counts as unknown (N19b-02), so the pack check gives 310 (exit 3) and the door gives 733 (exit 5); both are now named. 'A non-selected or branded object is refused by the default pipeline' had no mechanism, because N19b-02's filter refuses only rows with default_pipeline = false and this row is true. A DESIGN note now makes selection.toml narrow the default pipeline, refused with asset-source-not-default-pipeline (exit 3), observed naming the object and the list (requests to N19b-02 and N19-REF).

Aligned with BD-066's table: a connect becomes a class-S closure (not 'spherical or revolute') and a weld a fixed closure; a spring joint imports as an unactuated joint whose stiffness and springref are not mapped but listed at severity high (the design format has no joint spring). Validation (3) and the test (now robot_cassie_springs_passive_stiffness_listed) changed to match.

The control 'a foot sphere dropped (the end-effector count changes)' could not fire, because BD-066 infers no end effector; the field-coverage diff and the loss-report and DesignId goldens now catch it. The loss-report hypothesis is aligned with BD-066: damping, frictionloss and armature are mapped, not lost; only the keyframe home is mapped and other keyframes are listed; the report says 'no contact law declared'.

'IMU and joint sensors mapped to native sensors with an assumed rate' contradicted BD-066, under which sensors are not mapped and each is listed with the card that would fit. Damping, frictionloss and armature are mapped, and force ranges are card overrides.
Loss-report hypothesis aligned with BD-066 (damping, frictionloss and armature are mapped; only the keyframe home is mapped).
Loss-report hypothesis aligned with BD-066 (damping, frictionloss and armature are mapped, not lost).
Loss-report hypothesis aligned with BD-066 (force ranges and armature are overrides on the bound card; damping and frictionloss are joint-side).
Loss-report hypothesis aligned with BD-066 (damping, frictionloss and armature are mapped, not lost).

'Foot collision geometry mapped to a foot patch with a stated patch radius' contradicted BD-066, which infers no end effector or contact law (stage 1 gives 121 until one is declared). The test robot_h1_foot_patch_mapping_reported could not pass and is replaced by robot_h1_foot_geometry_no_law_inferred; the damping, frictionloss and armature hypothesis is aligned.

The knee self-collision validation (robot_spot_knee_range_self_collision_reported) needs A-13, but the bead had no dependency on it; added BD-104 (M1, no cycle) and named `frob analyze self-collision`. The 'position-dependent transmission modulus table' was replaced, because BD-066 maps gear as a constant ratio; the manifest, not the importer's loss report, records that the linkage ratio varies. Damping, frictionloss and armature aligned with BD-066.

'Cameras become sensors with frame, rate and clock' contradicted BD-066 (no camera element is mapped; sensors are listed), so they are now expected loss-report entries. Validation (3), the tip-over margin, had no definition and no test: it is now defined (distance from the projected centre of mass to the support polygon, with the payload from the manifest), and robot_stretch3_tipover_margin_reported is added.

'The importer maps rollers to roller-wheel with the angle recovered' contradicted BD-066 (no contact law is inferred). The roller angle is now recovered by this bead's validation and stored in the manifest, and a prescribed planar base becomes a manifest finding, not an importer loss entry. The arm's rank 6 is checked at a generic sample with rational cos and sin, not at the reference pose, which for a tucked arm may be singular.

Acceptance and the three tests required the same DesignId for the degree, inertia and Euler rewrites, which cannot hold when a rewrite writes new decimals (pi/2 for 90 degrees). Now atom-by-atom agreement within one unit in the last stored digit, as its own Considerations said; the tests are renamed *_same_atoms and the log line adjusted.

'Mapped to an actuator card with a position loop, the gain carried' contradicted BD-066, under which every MJCF actuator binds a generic assumed card and kp/kv are controller assumptions that are listed, not carried. Text and robot_op3_position_servo_mapping aligned.

zoo_quad_mammal_policy_tie_counterexample tested that 'the weight-sharing constructor refuses Γ_mech', but N13-16 makes that a compile-time type barrier (mech_group_cannot_tie) with no runtime refusal. The test now checks the lidar variant's ObsGroup (order 2) and its free-weight count (32,768 against 16,384). Added the missing dependency N13-14 for the algebra.irreps row of its known-answer table (M1, no cycle).

The 90,704-byte row and its unit test needed the byte model and sim.estimate (N17a-07, BD-219, M2) in an M1 bead. The row now carries NEG-30's blocked = milestone, due = M2. Control (c) (the 30-link G1 imported without a reduced block) needed NEG-32 and N14b-34, which were not dependencies; both added (M1, no cycle), and the command and the mass-dropped refusal (IMPORT_MASS_DROPPED, exit 3) are named. Control (a) now applies to the @g1 preset, since the default instance has no mass window.

'Γ_mech trivial with the payload' and control (a), assert_mech: C2 refused, contradicted BD-102 and N13-21, under which a payload reduces only Γ_obs. Now Γ_obs is trivial with the payload and Γ_mech stays C₂; the control asserts assert_obs: C2 (refused with 109), and the same variant with assert_mech: C2 is accepted.

Named the referee over-capacity refusal, FROB-REF-721 (exit 5; observed 24, required 21; BD-080). The e2e `sim run` gained --key and the full form; the phylum plan line now uses the row's --designs and --worlds-per-design inputs.

The forward-sensor breaker row was conditional ('C₂ if a wheel lies on the forward axis, nothing otherwise'), so the golden had no value. With wheels at 90°, 210° and 330° the reflection axes are 90°, 30° and 150°, none along +x, so Γ_obs is trivial with the sensor mount as breaker; that is now stated.

Control (c), a ratio +1 tie 'refused with FROB-REF-110', could not be refused: the tie is still one constraint on four passive coordinates, so mobility stays 3, and 110 is for mobility below one. Now the differential-law row catches it: on the (+10°, −10°) pose pair the closure has no solution.

Applied S-05's request after checking N13-25 and N13-26: the module group is the half-turn about the steer axis (K = C₂ with zero trail, trivial with trail), not a 'mirror'. Stage 5 and acceptance had expected 'the nested structure reported', which analyze.symmetry never reports; the nested group is N13-26's (M4, Frontier). Stage 5 now asserts D₄ of order 8 with no factor for the half-turn, and the test is renamed zoo_swerve4_module_half_turn_not_a_factor.

requests.what: Mark the uncentred row of registries/cards/GB-04.toml (printed 0.48 µm) with `stale-as-control: E7-K1` (a TOML comment on that line), and say so in the Technical approach and in gb_04's check. Otherwise NEG-03's E7-K1 entry (\b0\.48 ?[µμu]m in scope cell|offset|anchor|spacing, scanned from M0) fires on the card file, which is in the walk set.

Mark the small-angle row of registries/cards/GB-05.toml (printed 0.57 m for d = 0.10 m) with `stale-as-control: E7-K2` from GB-05's own milestone (M1). Otherwise NEG-03's E7-K2 entry (\b0\.57 ?m\b in scope sideways|lateral|shift, scanned from M0) fires: the engine has no negative condition and cannot see the 0.55 m beside it.

Write the stale entries of E7-K1 and E7-K2 as NEG-14 step 3 now states them: E7-K1 { pattern = "\\b0\\.48 ?[µμu]m", scope = "cell|offset|anchor|spacing" }; E7-K2 { pattern = "\\b0\\.57 ?m\\b", scope = "sideways|lateral|shift" }.

NEG-19 now relies on it for google-scanned-objects.

ZOO-humanoid's 'Dense per-world bytes at C = 64, R = 320 = 90,704' row now carries blocked = milestone, due = M2 (NEG-30's field). As the M2 owner of sim.estimate, remove the field by a dated amendment in the change that lands `--workload H`, so that zoo_goldens step 6 evaluates the row through `frob sim estimate --workload H --json`.

The swerve-4 paragraph (a) still says 'each module has its own mirror'. N13-25 and N13-26 compute the half-turn about the steer axis (K = C₂ with zero caster trail, trivial with trail), and analyze.symmetry reports only the hub group D₄. ZOO-swerve-4 now says so; align the template's text.
